newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico IMSS jobs up 64,000 in first half February.
newsitem.headline: Mexico IMSS jobs up 64,000 in first half February.

text.p: The number of permanently insured workers affiliated to Mexico's Social Security Institute (IMSS) grew by 64,000 during the first two weeks of February, Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo said on Monday.
"Just during the first two weeks of February, the number of permanently insured workers at the IMSS rose by more than 64,000 workers," Zedillo told a meeting of the Confederation of Mexican Workers.
Zedillo said that all the jobs lost during Mexico's 1994-1995 economic crisis had now been recovered and that the government was focusing on creating new jobs.
Zedillo cited recent unemployment figures of 4.5 percent in January as evidence of a jobs recovery. Unemployment in January of 1996 was 6.4 percent.
At the end of 1996, there were 9.16 million workers affiliated with the IMSS, according to government figures.
